# 18. Governance, Intellectual Property, and Licensing

## 18.1 Specification License

This specification is published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license. Any party MAY reproduce, excerpt, translate, or build derivative specifications from this document, provided they attribute the source and do not assert exclusivity over the underlying specification text.

## 18.2 Reference Implementation License

The reference implementation (schemas, reference codec, test harness, adversarial PCAPs) is published under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The Apache 2.0 patent grant extends to any contribution accepted into the reference implementation repository.

## 18.3 Patent Posture

The author, on behalf of Specter Point Intelligence, LLC, asserts no patent claims against good-faith implementations of this specification. Implementers of O-CPS are on notice that third parties may hold patents applicable to the underlying technologies (C-V2X, ITS-G5, SCMS); this specification grants no rights with respect to those patents. A defensive patent pool SHOULD be convened as adoption proceeds.

## 18.4 Governance Process

Evolution of O-CPS is governed by a lightweight change-proposal process. Any party MAY submit a change proposal to the public repository. Proposals are merged by rough consensus of the active implementer community, with an editorial veto reserved to the editor of record to preserve normative coherence. The intent is to transfer governance to an established standards body (IEEE-SA, ISO TC 22 SC 31, or SAE) once three independent conformant implementations are in public deployment.

## 18.5 Trademark

“Strynex” is a trademark of Specter Point Intelligence, LLC, applied only to the reference implementation and branded overlay (Slipstream Mode). Use of the term “O-CPS” in conformance claims is governed only by the conformance-class framework of §17 and is not subject to trademark gating.
